correctness.rationale: For n>=3 a core indicator a_i and pendant indicator b_i define an ordinary P3-convex vertex set exactly when any a_i=0 has a_{i-1}+a_{i+1}+b_i<=1. For a nonconstant core, this forbids cyclic 101, giving exactly m positive 1-runs separated by m 0-runs of lengths >=2. Stars-and-bars counts (n/m)*binom(t-1,m-1)*binom(n-t-m-1,m-1) labelled cores; exactly n-2m pendant vertices are independently selectable. Together with all-zero and all-one cores this proves the bivariate B_n(x,y) identity for every n. Cyclic overlap transfer matrix gives characteristic lambda*(lambda^3-(1+z)^2 lambda^2+z(1+z)^2 lambda-z(1+z)) and stated scalar recurrence with formal seeds Q0=3,Q1=(1+z)^2,Q2=(1+z)^4-2z(1+z)^2. Independent adjacency brute-forcing verified each coefficient for n=3..8, totals 22,64,184,524,1488,4224; finite checks only corroborate infinite combinatorial proof.

originality.rationale: The scalar specialization and third-order scalar recurrence coincide with OEIS A073313, a prior known integer sequence, and are explicitly NOT original. Dourado–Grippo–Lin–Protti (2026) develops counting ordinary P3-convex sets, with general hardness and particular family algorithms, but their accessible full article does not provide the cyclic sunlet core–leaf bivariate refinement. The source proof adds the nontrivial invariant that free pendants depend solely on number of core runs, not their lengths; neither scalar OEIS data nor general tree algorithms imply joint coefficients. Best-of-knowledge O passes for the joint polynomial only.
